comparison: Perfect agreement on kinetic analysis claims (C3, C54-C63). Both OpenEval and peer reviewers conclude that β-domain assembly is rate-limiting and that the kinetic data strongly supports this conclusion. Reviewer 2 explicitly affirms the findings are consistent with the model.

Perfect agreement on nanodisc experiments (C5, C67-C74). Both evaluations find the evidence compelling that a single Bam complex is sufficient for EspP assembly. Reviewer 3 explicitly states the nanodisc experiments provide compelling evidence, matching OpenEval's assessment.

Perfect agreement on translocation evidence (C49-C53). Both evaluations accept the proteinase K protection experiments as strong evidence for complete passenger domain translocation. Reviewer 3 explicitly affirms the PK-digestion experiments and notes appropriate controls were included.

Strong agreement on sufficiency of BamABCDE and SurA (C2, C37-C39, C46-C48), though peer review also includes accessory protein claims (C40-C45) that OpenEval addresses separately. All three peer reviewers call this a major accomplishment and significant contribution, aligning with OpenEval's SUPPORTED evaluation.

Strong agreement on background and literature claims (C1, C6-C30, C95-C102). Both evaluations accept these as well-supported by citations. Peer review notes minor framing issues (oversimplification about virulence factors) and presentation suggestions, but does not challenge the factual content.

Disagreement on generalizability of improved Bam complex preparation method (C36, C91). OpenEval finds the activity difference well-supported, while Reviewer 2 expresses uncertainty about whether this is lab-specific and recommends toning down claims about the novel method.

Significant disagreement on folding-deficient mutants and energy requirements (C4, C64-C66). OpenEval finds evidence that folding is not the sole driver as well-supported, while Reviewer 3 questions whether the in vitro system accurately reflects in vivo requirements, noting problematic discrepancies between in vivo and in vitro behavior.

Agreement on catalytic turnover (C43-C45). OpenEval finds these claims supported by substrate addition experiments. Peer review includes these claims in their broader acceptance of the reconstitution system as a major accomplishment.

Agreement on accessory protein roles (C40-C41). OpenEval finds evidence that BamB and BamC have accessory roles and that Skp inhibits assembly. Peer review includes these claims in their overall acceptance of the reconstitution findings.

Agreement on supporting observations and discussion points (C85-C90). Both evaluations accept these as reasonable interpretations. OpenEval finds them supported by citations and data, while peer review accepts them as part of the discussion with only minor presentation suggestions.

Agreement on background claims about EspP structure and rationale (C31-C35). OpenEval finds these provide important foundation for the experimental approach. Peer review includes these in their acceptance of background claims, with only minor presentation suggestions.

Partial overlap on energy-independent assembly (C4, C75). OpenEval finds strong evidence for energy-independent assembly from reconstitution experiments. Peer review's uncertainty (R5) focuses more on the folding-deficient mutants (C64-C66) rather than the basic energy independence claim, suggesting partial agreement.

Agreement on speculative mechanisms in discussion (C78-C80, C82-C84). Both evaluations accept these as reasonable interpretations and speculation. Peer review notes only minor presentation suggestions about claims based on negative evidence.

Agreement on speculative claims about Bam complex structure (C92-C94). Both evaluations accept these as reasonable speculation based on activity differences and preliminary data. Peer review includes these in their acceptance of discussion points.

Agreement on comparison to other translocation systems (C76-C77). Both evaluations accept these comparative claims. OpenEval notes they highlight the surprising nature of energy-independent assembly, while peer review accepts them as part of the discussion.
